chunks: And the Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me of this hadith, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, and 'Ali ibn Hadid, and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Hariz ibn 'Abd Allah, from Zurarah, who said:
Abu Ja'far عليه السلام said: Like the first hadith.

The Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, said: Whoever omits rinsing the mouth and sniffing water into the nose during wudu (ablution), his omission does not impair his taharah (ritual purity), except that he is leaving a merit.

key_terms.الِاسْتِنْشَاقَ: drawing water into the nose during wudu (ablution)
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), the ritual washing before salat (prayer)
key_terms.فَضْلًا: an additional merit or recommended excellence

ai.seo_question: Does leaving rinsing the mouth and nose in wudu invalidate the ablution?
ai.summary: This hadith indicates that the report here carries the same purport as the first hadith in the chapter. It also states that omitting al-madmada and al-istinshaq in wudu (ablution) does not invalidate ritual purity, though it means leaving a recommended merit.
